title: Agent Certificate v0 Ledger Seal Wire Shapes
description: The NETWORK-BOUNDARY wire shapes for the dedicated certificate build-ledger's seals, per C1 Ruling 2. Server-internal ledger persistence (raw chain_id, seq, previous/event/payload HMACs, HMAC key IDs, and raw seal roots) NEVER crosses this boundary and is deliberately unrepresentable here — those fields belong to build-item B2 under the single BE integration owner, not to this schema family. What crosses is the FIXED EXPECTED-STREAM PROJECTION: one entry for every expected stream family, with explicit states and absence invalid. The explicit B-v0 build-ledger profile is `traigent.cert_build_ledger.v0`: transition and receipt_event are sealed, while decision is empty_sealed. In v0 this signed projection participates in the signed unsigned-manifest chain and G1 evidence binding; it is not independent proof of B1, ledger completeness, ordering, event inclusion, splice resistance, or omission resistance. B1 remains abstained, and only D2 and G1 print in v0. Event counts and terminal sequence values are EXCLUDED from the v0 wire shape. The public projection is limited to seal_ref, chain_schema_version, build_session_ref, the fixed family/status/opaque-root entries, and the role-separated seal_statement_digest. Root instance is one SealStatementV0.

StreamFamilyV0.description: Closed vocabulary of the three expected stream families, derived from the three supplied chain-enabled Planner-V2 table families. The evidence establishes 'missing cross-table uniqueness/order enforcement, not exactly three logical chains' (C6 Ruling 1 struck the 'exactly three parallel chains' inference); this enum fixes the EXPECTED projection universe at the boundary, not the internal chain count.

StreamStateV0.description: Explicit per-stream chain status. NEVER null or absent — 'chain_status must be an explicit enum, never NULL/absent (absence is indistinguishable from omitted, one of the mandated fixtures)' (C1 Ruling 2, conceded). legacy_unsealed labels pre-chain sessions ('legacy NULL rows remain legacy/unsealed, as binding evidence requires'); legacy/unsealed sessions are REFUSED issuance, never silently downgraded (C6 Ruling 1, conceded). not_applicable is narrowly defined: admissible only where the stream family is structurally absent for the session type per the declared certificate-scope manifest, never as a default.

NonZeroRootCommitmentV0.description: An opaque, non-sentinel root commitment. The all-zero digest is reserved as a synthetic/unsealed marker and is not admissible in a B-v0 public seal projection; this shape does not make the root independently recomputable.

StreamProjectionEntryV0.description: One expected-stream projection entry: family + explicit state + (when sealed) the opaque root commitment. A root commitment is an OPAQUE issuer-committed value: 'Signing a hash of an HMAC root lets a relying party verify that the issuer signed an opaque value. It does not prove deletion, truncation, reordering, or omission resistance' (C1 Ruling 2). root_commitment is REQUIRED for sealed/empty_sealed states and FORBIDDEN for legacy_unsealed/not_applicable, so a legacy stream can never masquerade as sealed (fixture class: legacy-NULL-chain presented as chained).

ExpectedStreamProjectionV0.description: The fixed expected-stream projection: EXACTLY one entry per expected stream family, keyed so absence is schema-invalid ('Absence is invalid'). A missing stream is the 'missing-stream' relying-party fixture class and must be unrepresentable, not merely discouraged.

SealStatementV0.description: The terminal seal statement wire shape — the exact object claim B1's template refers to ('The issuer signed this seal statement'). Binds subject/session, the explicit B-v0 build-ledger profile, and the fixed expected-stream projection into one canonical statement whose digest the issuer signs. Session binding uses an opaque build-session ref; issuer/environment/tenant scoping of the namespace 'were not supplied' (C1 Ruling 2), so this shape does NOT claim the ref alone is a globally safe namespace — splice resistance is a non-claim. The relying party verifies the signed public projection but cannot independently recompute Backend HMAC history or prove completeness/omission resistance.

seal_ref.description: Server-assigned opaque seal identifier; the named seal of claim B1's 'ledger entries committed by seal X' scope (C6 Ruling 3(i)).

chain_schema_version.description: Explicit B-v0 build-ledger profile for new-session rows. This exact version identifies the stream-state mapping transition=sealed, receipt_event=sealed, decision=empty_sealed.

build_session_ref.description: Opaque subject/session binding for the sealed streams.

seal_statement_digest.description: Role-separated SHA-256 digest over the canonical v0 seal-statement projection: UTF8('traigent.agent_certificate.seal_statement.v1') || 0x00 || fp2(JCS) of this object with seal_statement_digest excluded. The self-digest field is excluded from its own preimage to avoid circularity. This is the digest claim B1 binds and the signed unsigned manifest covers; a relying party MUST recompute and compare it before accepting the projection.

allOf.description: B-v0 has exactly two real sealed streams (transition and receipt_event) and one explicitly empty sealed stream (decision). This fixed profile prevents a synthetic/all-empty projection from entering the certificate wire contract.

LedgerEntryCommitmentV0.description: A typed canonical event commitment reference for evidence binding: stream family + entry commitment digest. Carries NO raw chain_id, seq, HMAC, or HMAC key ID (server-internal, C1 Ruling 2). An entry commitment proves the issuer committed to a canonical event encoding; it does not prove the event's content is true nor that neighbouring events exist.
